title: 💻 Nadella explains why he offered 60,000 Microsoft employees the chance to leave!
body: 💻 Nadella explains why he offered 60,000 Microsoft employees the chance to leave!

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained on Wednesday why the company last October offered voluntary departure packages to about 60,000 employees — more than a quarter of its roughly 223,000 employees — instead of laying them off in a new round of cuts. Nadella said, during the 'DealBook' summit in a conversation with journalist Andrew Ross Sorkin, that the goal is for everyone to feel they have 'agency', because talk of the AI revolution has created great anxiety among employees about their fate. He explained that Microsoft is not replacing employees with AI, but reorganizing work so every employee uses AI and manages its agents, until each employee becomes an 'agent manager' instead of doing the work directly. He gave the example of a team building the 'CoWork' agent in Microsoft 365 apps, with just 11 developers who mastered using AI, who have become 'building a software factory that builds the product, not building the product themselves'. Employees must decide before the deadline in early December.

Simply put: the message to employees is: either learn to work with AI and manage it, or take compensation and leave by choice; and the company wants to become an AI-first company without looking like it is firing people.
Would you accept a voluntary departure offer, or learn to work with AI?
